reasons: Cited text supports every preferred parameter: § 22.1 caps audits at 'no more than once in any twelve-month period', requires 'at least thirty days' prior written notice', normal business hours, off-site where practicable, and an independent auditor bound by confidentiality.

§ 22.2 allocates audit costs to Vendor unless underpayment exceeds five percent (matching the preferred 5% flip) and expressly prohibits Vendor/auditor direct access to Customer systems, so no walk-away trigger (unlimited/unannounced audits or remote access) is present.

The failing 'audit frequency limited' deterministic check is a plausible lexical false negative (word-form 'twelve-month' rather than a digit); the paragraph text plainly imposes a hard 1-per-12-month cap, so the check does not undercut the compliant conclusion.
Absence of a redline and counterparty comment is correct for a compliant finding retained as internal evidence; no actionable edit is required and none was proposed.
